caption: The video captures a tabletop physics demonstration set against a whiteboard, with a person's hand in a striped sleeve extending an index finger that rests on a round knob labeled FREQUENCY on a white function-generator box. The box's red LED readout climbs in discrete steps during the clip. It rises from 2.08 through 2.11, 2.16, 2.18, 2.25, and 2.28 toward 2.30 while the finger stays in light contact with the control. To the right, a vertical coil spring suspends a flat circular metal disk tied by a string loop. The disk oscillates up and down in front of a hand-drawn vertical scale marked with positive and negative ticks around a horizontal reference line. A blue driver coil with binding posts sits beneath the spring, and a metal rod stands at the far right. The camera and background remain fixed throughout the excerpt.
relations: Finger turning the FREQUENCY knob makes the red LED readout climb in discrete steps.
The rising drive frequency feeds the blue coil, which couples to the suspended disk-spring system.
The metal disk oscillates vertically about the horizontal reference line as the readout increases.
Background, hand-drawn scale, and right-side rod stay fixed while the readout and disk motion change.
